Welcome to the Executive Summary of the Data Product Framework. In seven slides, we show how a business idea becomes a verified, governed data product in BigQuery and BigQuery Knowledge Catalog—with sample screenshots of the actual Use-Case Definition, BRD/PRD, and Output Data Product documents.
01 · THE EXECUTIVE PROBLEM & SOLUTION

Unchecked pipelines silently drift from business rules while technical tests stay green

1 · WHAT THE BUSINESS ASKS Business Intent

Plain-English commercial rules

Finance and Sales leaders ask for trusted metrics defined in business terms, not SQL code.

EXAMPLE BUSINESS RULE (R-11)
“Cancelled or unfulfilled sales orders must never appear in monthly net sales.”
  • Owned and approved by the business sponsor
  • Clear rules for freshness, history, and privacy
  • Scored for value and ease before engineering starts
Artefact: Use-Case Definition & BRD / PRD
2 · WHERE PIPELINES FAIL Silent Semantic Drift

Hand-coded translations lose intent

When specs live in static slide decks and SQL is hand-written, business meaning breaks silently.

GREEN PIPELINE · WRONG REVENUE
A schema check passes (net_sales IS NOT NULL), yet amended orders are double-counted.
  • Documents drift from production SQL on day two
  • Technical tests check column types, not business logic
  • Downstream consumers discover errors in board meetings
Result: Broken executive trust & manual reconciliations
3 · HOW DPF ENFORCES TRUST 5 Machine Gates

Signed playback to proven output

The framework compiles approved requirements directly into code, sandbox tests, and catalog metadata.

CRYPTOGRAPHIC BUILD PROOF (G4)
Every requirement scenario runs against sandbox data before BigQuery views can be published.
  • Sponsor signs plain-English semantics.md playback (G1)
  • Approved skills generate SQL, Terraform, and tests (G2–G3)
  • Live SLO breaches open a governed change proposal
Artefact: Signed Output Data Product & Catalog Entry
Executive Guarantee: No engineering starts without a scored use case and plain-English BRD (Gate G0), and no table publishes without passing every business scenario (Gate G4).
Step 1 → 3
Slide 2 contrasts traditional data pipelines with the Data Product Framework. Traditional pipelines test whether columns are null; our framework proves that every business rule—like excluding cancelled orders or preserving historical customer segments—passes in sandbox before publication.
02 · THE VIRTUOUS CIRCULAR LIFECYCLE

Every data product and change moves clockwise through six stages and five automated gates

STAGES 1 & 2 · DEFINE & DESIGN Gates G0 & G1

Lock business meaning before writing code

Sponsors score the use case and author a plain-English BRD or PRD (G0). The technical design is translated back into a plain-English playback (semantics.md) for business sign-off (G1).

STAGES 3 & 4 · COMPOSE & BUILD Gates G2 & G3

Assemble approved skills and generate code

The pipeline composer selects pre-tested methodology skills (Kimball star schema, SCD2 history) and verifies every handoff (G2). Deterministic templates render Dataform SQL, Terraform, and test suites (G3).

STAGES 5 & 6 · TEST, PUBLISH & MONITOR Gate G4 & Δ Loop

Prove every scenario and guard production SLOs

Sandbox execution proves every BRD scenario and binds cryptographic digests before publishing to BigQuery and Knowledge Catalog (G4). Live drift or SLO breaches open an OpenSpec Δ back at Stage 1.

Why it is a circle, not a one-way pipe: Production schema drift, volume anomalies, or changing business rules automatically trigger an OpenSpec change proposal that re-enters Gate G0.
Self-Healing Governance Loop
Slide 3 presents the circular 6-stage lifecycle. Notice how Define and Design sit at the top (guarded by G0 and G1), Compose and Build sit on the right and bottom (guarded by G2 and G3), and Test and Monitor sit on the left (guarded by G4), feeding back into Define through the OpenSpec change loop.

04 · SAMPLE DOCUMENT 2 OF 3 · BRD & PRD SPECIFICATIONS ENFORCED BY GATE G0

Approved use cases become plain-English BRD or PRD specs with testable scenarios

Direct Compilation to Test: Scenario AX-12 (Given order SO-1003 is CANCELLED, When published, Then excluded from net_sales) compiles directly into a Gate G4 SQL assertion.
📘 4a-brd.pdf · BRD-SALES-002: Change History, Purpose, Exceptions & Access Click sheet to zoom PDF ↗
OPTION A · 4A-BRD.PDF BRD-SALES-002

1. Business Requirements Document (BRD)

Written with the business owner via author-brd. Captures purpose, metric definitions, and commercial trade-offs (e.g. moving from 15-minute to hourly refresh to avoid CDC costs).

OPTION B · 4B-PRD.PDF Same Rubric

2. Product Requirements Document (PRD)

Product-led organisations can use the companion PRD template (Product Summary, Users & Use Cases, Quality Bar). Both templates validate against the exact same brd.yaml contract.

GATE G0 · 13 SCENARIOS Zero Tech Jargon

3. Testable Given / When / Then rules

Every requirement (R-1 to R-13) carries a concrete scenario. Gate G0 rejects the spec if it contains technical terms like BigQuery, Dataform, or partition.

Gate G0 Enforcement: The specification must be 100% readable by a business owner while remaining structured enough to generate automated acceptance tests.
Slide 5 shows both the filled Business Requirements Document (4a-brd.pdf) two-page spread and the side-by-side comparison with the Product Requirements Document (4b-prd.pdf), plus a close-up of Requirement R-11 and its Given/When/Then scenario (AX-12).

SECTION 3 & 4 · LIVE DATA & CATALOG 9 Glossary Terms

2. Verified BigQuery rows & Knowledge Catalog

Proves point-in-time segment history (Acme Pty Ltd stays SMB in March and becomes ENTERPRISE in June), binds 9 glossary terms in BigQuery Knowledge Catalog, and masks PII.

CRYPTOGRAPHIC BINDING 13 / 13 Passed

3. Unbroken digest & live SLO monitoring

Publication is blocked unless spec_digest and build_digest match the tested sandbox build. Live monitors enforce the 06:00 AEST daily close and 60-minute freshness SLO.

What Consumers Receive: Governed BigQuery authorized views, rich business definitions in BigQuery Knowledge Catalog, masked contact PII, and guaranteed service levels.
